objections.claim_attacked: title: GRT DRC-error cap (10000) hides congestion hotspots and macro-overlap errors
objections.objection: The record itself notes the placement heatmap has a similar vertical line, so the vertical stop in GRT DRCs is not uniquely attributable to the 10000 cap; the title asserts a cap-caused localization artifact that the thread leaves ambiguous between the error cap and a physical placement boundary.

objections.claim_attacked: hypothesis: errors in macro-overlap / hard-to-fix areas fall outside the reported window until the design is reduced
objections.objection: The record never specifies the ordering of the first 10000 errors or shows that omitted macro-overlap errors were excluded because of their hard-to-fix nature rather than simply appearing later in the scan; deltaDebug.py reducing the design could change which errors are reported independently of any selection rule.

mechanism_check: N-D — chosen_intervention is not stated, so there is no intervention whose mechanism can be checked against the observation and post_state.
evidence_check: ASSERT — post_state is only the issue being closed, with no confirmation that random-sampling or most-interesting selection was implemented and no before/after metric.
attribution_check: ABSENT — the record contains no direct_quote block, so there is no named participant, date, or locator to assess.
missing_from_story: The actual ordering or selection rule used for the first 10000 GRT DRC errors, and whether it was changed.
A direct comparison of the vertical line against the placement map to distinguish a cap artifact from a physical boundary.
Before/after evidence that random sampling or 'most-interesting' selection was implemented, plus any resulting DRC-report behavior.
What 'closed as completed' meant with 0 comments, and whether any PR, commit, or maintainer decision accompanied it.
most_defensible_part: The concrete 10000-cap and the deltaDebug.py observation that macro-overlap errors were absent from the first 10000 until the design was reduced.
